items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A girl pushes a wall till she is tired; a boy pushes a trolley 3 m. Who did more work?

Lifting bags gives **W = F × s**, the **joule** and work as the **area under a force–displacement graph**. A wall, a carried box and a satellite show **zero work**; a trolley, a goalkeeper and a sliding box show **positive and negative work**.

A cricket ball introduces **energy**, and a pushed trolley gives the **work–energy theorem** and **K = ½mv²**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• force, net force and Newton's second law, F = ma

• displacement and its direction

• the equation of motion v² = u² + 2as

• converting km/h to m/s

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Calculate work done (W = Fs) and identify zero, positive and negative work.

**2.** Calculate kinetic energy (½mv²) and relate work to change in kinetic energy.

**3.** Solve numericals on work and kinetic energy.

• Left: a girl pushes a brick wall; 10 minutes later she is still pushing and is very tired.

• Right: a boy pushes a shopping trolley **3 m**.

**Answer to Question 1**

**Answer to Question 2**

**Answer to Question 3**

The **wall did not move**; the **trolley moved 3 m**.

**What this shows**

A 5 kg bag of wheat lifted slowly: (a) one bag through 1 m, (b) three bags together through 1 m, (c) one bag through 3 m.

**Answer to Question 4**

**3W.** You need three times the force over the same distance.

**Answer to Question 5**

**3W.** The same force over three times the distance.

**Answer to Question 6**

The **force**, and **how far the object moves in the direction of the force**.

**What this shows**

(a) A constant force of 20 N against displacement, from 0 to 3 m. The area under the line is shaded.

**Answer to Question 7**

W = 20 × 3 = **60 J**.

**Answer to Question 8**

20 × 3 = **60**. It is the **same as the work done**.

items.prompt: A shopkeeper pushes a 15 kg carton across the floor with a force of 50 N, and it moves 4 m in the direction of the push. The work done by the shopkeeper on the carton is
True or false? Lifting a 10 N bag slowly through 2 m needs the same work as lifting a 20 N bag slowly through 1 m.
options: False: the heavier bag needs more work
False: the longer lift needs more work

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: W = 50 × 4 = **200 J**. The mass is not needed.

**On Question 2**

**A**: **true**. 10 × 2 = 20 J and 20 × 1 = 20 J.

items.prompt: Look at graph (b). The force on a cart grows steadily from 0 to 8 N while the cart moves 4 m. The work done is

items.text:
**On this question**

**B**: work = **area of the triangle** = ½ × 4 × 8 = **16 J**. (A) treats the force as 8 N all the way.

items.text:
**What this shows**

(a) A girl pushing a wall. (b) A girl holding up a box with force F while walking forwards. (c) A satellite in a circular orbit; the Earth's pull F points to the centre.

**Answer to Question 9**

**s = 0**, so W = F × 0 = **0**. She does **no work** on the wall.

**Answer to Question 10**

Her muscles keep tightening and relaxing, which uses up energy in her body. But **no work is done on the wall**.

**Answer to Question 11**

**No.** It moves only forwards, so there is no displacement in the direction of F. Her force does **no work** on the box.

**Answer to Question 12**

**Zero.** The force is **perpendicular** to the motion at every point. This is why the satellite's speed does not change.

items.text:
**What this shows**

(a) A push on a trolley. (b) A goalkeeper's glove pushing a ball backwards as it slows down. (c) Friction on a box sliding to a stop. Each shows the force and the displacement s.

**Answer to Question 13**

**Positive**: W = + F × s. The push **speeds the trolley up**.

**Answer to Question 14**

The force and the displacement are opposite, so W = − 200 × 0.15 = **− 30 J**.

**Answer to Question 15**

It **slows the ball down** and stops it.

**Answer to Question 16**

**Negative.** Friction acts opposite to the box's displacement, so it slows the box down.

options: lifting a bag onto a shelf
a porter standing still with a load on his head
pushing a bicycle up a slope

items.prompt: Is the work done by gravity positive, negative or zero on (i) a coconut falling from a tree, (ii) a ball thrown upwards while it rises, (iii) a ball rolling along a level floor?
A cyclist brakes. The brakes push the bicycle backwards with a force of 150 N while it moves 6 m forwards. The work done by the brakes is

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**B**: the load does not move, so **s = 0**.

**On Question 2**

**A**: (i) **positive** (ii) **negative** (iii) **zero**: gravity acts down, and the ball moves sideways.

**On Question 3**

**B**: the force is opposite to the displacement: W = − 150 × 6 = **− 900 J**.

**What this shows**

• Left: a fielder throws the ball hard.

• Right: the ball hits the stumps and knocks them over.

**Answer to Question 17**

**Yes.** It applies a force, and the stumps move.

**Answer to Question 18**

items.text:
**What this shows**

A trolley of mass m moving at speed u, pushed by a constant net force F. After a displacement s, its speed is v.

**Answer to Question 19**

**W = F × s.**

**Answer to Question 20**

F = ma, so **W = ma × s**.

**Answer to Question 21**

**a × s = (v² − u²) ÷ 2.**

**Answer to Question 22**

W = m × (v² − u²) ÷ 2 = **½mv² − ½mu²**.

script.x: Show the trolley. Pointer 1 sets it up.
Build the result on the board with Questions 19 to 22. Answers are on pointers 2 to 5.
Show the key idea.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 23**

W = 10 × 5 = **50 J**, so it gains **50 J** of kinetic energy.

**Answer to Question 24**

½ × 4 × v² = 50, so v² = 25 and **v = 5 m/s**.

**Answer to Question 25**

Twice as fast: (2v)² = 4v², so **4 times**. Twice the mass: **2 times**.

**Answer to Question 26**

**No.** m and v² are never negative. Like work, it has **no direction**.

items.prompt: A cricket ball of mass 0.2 kg is bowled at 144 km/h. Its kinetic energy is
Objects A and B have masses m and 4m and the same kinetic energy. The ratio of their speeds, vA : vB, is
True or false? A car moving at a steady 60 km/h on a straight road has kinetic energy, but the net work done on it is zero.
options: True: its kinetic energy does not change
False: it has kinetic energy, so work is being done
False: the engine does positive net work
True: it has no kinetic energy

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: 144 km/h = 144 × 5 ÷ 18 = 40 m/s. K = ½ × 0.2 × 40² = **160 J**. (B) forgets to convert km/h.

**On Question 2**

**B**: ½m vA² = ½(4m) vB², so vA² = 4vB² and **vA = 2vB**.

**On Question 3**

**A**: **true**. Its speed does not change, so its kinetic energy does not change, and the net work done on it is zero.
